title: OpenMTB-Audit: Exposing Over-Refusal and Clinical Expert Perspectives in LLM-Based Molecular Tumor Board Safety Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2610.01497v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Molecular tumor boards integrate genomic findings, clinical context, and therapeutic evidence to support precision oncology. As AI enters this workflow, a key safety challenge is distinguishing truly unsupported recommendations from evidence-supported options that still require oncologist review because of incomplete information, poor ECOG performance status, or other clinical caveats. We introduce OpenMTB-Audit, an open-source benchmark of 500 synthetic non-small cell lung cancer cases spanning five adversarial error categories and four safety labels: Supported, Partially Supported, Unsupported, and Insufficient Information. Across eight large language model configurations, we identify pervasive over-refusal: all LLM configurations failed to retain the Partially Supported label in 83.3-100% of true Partially Supported cases, achieving high aggregate safety scores through label collapse rather than clinically calibrated reasoning. translated_title: OpenMTB-Audit：揭示基于大语言模型的分子肿瘤会诊安全性评估中的过度拒绝现象与临床专家视角
translated_abstract: 分子肿瘤会诊整合基因组学发现、临床背景与治疗证据，以支持精准肿瘤学。随着人工智能进入这一工作流程，一个关键的安全挑战是区分真正缺乏依据的推荐与那些虽有证据支持、但因信息不完整、ECOG体能状态较差或其他临床注意事项而仍需肿瘤科医生审查的选项。我们提出了OpenMTB-Audit，这是一个开源基准数据集，包含500个合成的非小细胞肺癌病例，涵盖五种对抗性错误类别和四个安全标签：支持、部分支持、不支持、信息不足。通过对八种大语言模型配置的评估，我们发现了普遍存在的过度拒绝现象：所有大语言模型配置在83.3%至100%的真正“部分支持”病例中未能保留“部分支持”标签，它们通过标签坍缩而非临床校准的推理获得了较高的总体安全评分。为进一步……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究发布了包含500个非小细胞肺癌合成病例的开源基准OpenMTB-Audit，揭示大语言模型在分子肿瘤会诊安全评估中普遍存在“过度拒绝”现象——所有模型在83.3%至100%的“部分支持”病例中无法保留该标签，依靠标签坍缩而非临床校准推理来获得高安全评分。
en_tdlr: OpenMTB-Audit, an open-source benchmark of 500 synthetic non-small cell lung cancer cases, reveals pervasive over-refusal in LLM-based molecular tumor board safety evaluation, where all eight LLM configurations collapse the "Partially Supported" label in 83.3–100% of true Partially Supported cases, achieving high aggregate safety scores through label collapse rather than clinically calibrated reasoning.
